title: Nushrratt Bharuccha Posted an RCB Victory Celebration. The Internet Heard a Puppy and Decided It Was a Scandal.
excerpt: A viral Instagram Story clip, a whimpering puppy at a friend's house, and a days-long harassment campaign that says more about social media in 2026 than it does about anyone in the video.
body:
Nushrratt Bharuccha did what millions of RCB fans did on the night of May 31: she recorded the television screen as Royal Challengers Bengaluru lifted the IPL 2026 trophy and posted it to her Instagram Stories.

Within hours, the internet had decided the clip contained something scandalous.

What Actually Happened

Users claimed to hear sounds in the background that they interpreted as moaning and slapping. The clip went viral — not for the cricket, but for what social media detectives believed was happening off-camera. Conspiracy theories multiplied. Screenshots circulated. And someone even issued a statement in Nushrratt's name that she never authorized.

After days of escalating speculation, Nushrratt addressed the controversy on Instagram Stories with photos, videos, and the kind of exhausted clarity that comes from watching the internet lose its mind over background audio.

The sound, she explained, was a puppy.

She had been watching the match at a friend's house. The friend's young puppy was crying during the recording. She shared a video from the same night, shot from a different angle, with the same sounds clearly audible — along with a photo of the puppy itself.

"Kuch logon ne hadh hi kar di hai," she wrote. "Ek puppy ke rone ki awaaz se itna bawaal mach gaya hai." Some people have crossed all limits. A puppy's crying has caused this much chaos.

The Receipts

Nushrratt posted multiple Instagram Stories to dismantle the narrative methodically:

A photo of the living room and television where she watched the match. A video from the same night made by her friend at the same time, from a different angle, with the identical background sounds. A photo of the puppy. And a direct response to the fake clarification someone had posted in her name.

"Fearing exactly what has happened, I was advised to delete that video, and I did," she wrote. "People, calm your wild thoughts down. Owning a mobile phone doesn't empower harassment. Do not misinterpret or follow blindly. Think and act responsibly."

The Bigger Problem

The Nushrratt Bharuccha episode is minor in isolation — an Instagram Story, some ambient noise, a puppy. But the mechanics of what happened reveal something deeply familiar about how the internet treats women in 2026.

An ambiguous audio clip was extracted from a temporary Story post. It was reposted, screenshotted, and analyzed by thousands of strangers. A sexual narrative was constructed and applied without evidence. And a woman was placed in the position of having to prove, with receipts and photographs, that the sounds in her video were an animal crying — not something the mob had fantasized about.

The fact that someone created a fake statement in her name — presumably to generate more engagement — adds another layer of manipulation that is increasingly common in the creator economy, where controversy is currency.

For Indian women in the public eye, the playbook is depressingly predictable. The cost of posting anything, even a cricket celebration, is the risk of having your content repurposed into someone else's salacious narrative.

What It Says About Digital Culture

The episode also highlights the speed at which misinformation travels on platforms designed for engagement over accuracy. A clip is posted. The original creator deletes it. But by then, screen recordings exist across X, Reddit, and WhatsApp. Context collapses. The person who made the content loses control of the narrative entirely.

Nushrratt handled it with clarity and composure — providing evidence, naming the manipulation, and refusing to perform shame. But the fact that she had to devote multiple Instagram Stories and several days to debunking a puppy video tells you everything about where we are.

The internet owes Nushrratt Bharuccha an apology. It probably owes the puppy one too.
